title: API Key Management

searches.query: "API Key Management" interview rotation compromised key storage
searches.result: success; exact-concept search executed, but independent frequency/rank/company evidence was insufficient; prompts are original production adaptations and technical decisions use checked primary sources

sources.title: System Design Primer: Security
sources.supportRationale: Core conceptual orientation checked during specification; its brief section explicitly needs updates and is not the sole protocol/crypto authority or evidence of interview frequency.

sources.title: OWASP: REST Security Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: API credentials, token/access controls, safe error/log handling and TLS; API keys alone are insufficient for every sensitive resource.

sources.title: OWASP: Secrets Management Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Credential bootstrap/distribution, least privilege, dynamic/static lifecycle, rotation and audit; no universal manager availability claim.

sources.title: OWASP: Cryptographic Storage Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Layered data protection, authenticated modes and key lifecycle; protection depends on attacker and access boundaries.

sources.title: OWASP: Authorization Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Least privilege, default denial and resource/action authorization on every request, with trusted enforcement and failure handling.

sources.title: IETF RFC 10017: OAuth 2.0 for Browser-Based Applications
sources.supportRationale: Browser OAuth threats and architectural boundaries including BFFs, checked as the published August 2026 BCP rather than an old draft.

scenarios.theme: A production partner key appears in a public log. Keep a rotation overlap?
scenarios.assumptions: There is evidence the credential is compromised. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies API Key Management to leaked key.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A production partner key appears in a public log. Keep a rotation overlap?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Revoke according to incident urgency, issue a scoped replacement through a protected path, remove/redact exposed copies where possible and investigate usag

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Immediate revocation can interrupt clients

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: A long convenience overlap leaves known stolen authority usable; removing the log alone cannot make copied bytes secret again.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to secrets, rest; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: Support wants to display a forgotten secret stored only as a verifier. What do you offer?
scenarios.assumptions: The system deliberately cannot recover the plaintext credential. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies API Key Management to show again.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Support wants to display a forgotten secret stored only as a verifier. What do you offer?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Offer authorized replacement/revocation and one-time protected delivery rather than pretending the verifier can be decrypted

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: The client must redeploy

scenarios.theme: A valid tenant A key submits work for tenant B. Where do you reject it?
scenarios.assumptions: The request body chooses a tenant independently of trusted key ownership. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies API Key Management to tenant header.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A valid tenant A key submits work for tenant B. Where do you reject it?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Resolve the credential’s scoped owner, verify the target resource/action and reject unauthorized tenant selection at the owning service.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Explicit delegation can support legitimate multi-tenant clients, but must be modeled

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Credential validity alone cannot authorize arbitrary caller-selected scope.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to authz, rest; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A mobile/browser bundle contains a privileged partner key. Is obfuscation enough?
scenarios.assumptions: Every distributed client can be inspected and the key authorizes sensitive server actions. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies API Key Management to public app.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A mobile/browser bundle contains a privileged partner key. Is obfuscation enough?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Remove privileged shared authority from the public bundle, revoke exposed credentials and use an appropriate trusted backend or supported per-client/user p

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: The replacement architecture adds identity/operations

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Public identifiers and limited nonsecret project keys can have other roles, but naming a privileged secret an API key does not make shipping it safe.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to browser, rest, secrets; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

publicDisclosure: Researched 2026-11-17. These are adapted production scenarios informed by concept-specific interview searches and the named references below. The System Design Primer provides core orientation where applicable; technical guarantees use the mapped primary sources. Exact interview frequency, rankings and company attribution were not independently verified. Security protocol and runtime examples state their assumptions; the questions test reasoning rather than a universal product recommendation.
